answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprint Rule. Each identity must reproduce a stable behavioural fingerprint—recurrent action sequences, resource-use ratios, and response latencies—across non-adjacent epochs. A tundra of sparse activity is tolerated, but persistent divergence triggers quarantine. Hollow identities built to mimic one epoch fail on recurrence. Any nectar of profit gained is forfeited when the mismatch surfaces. Attackers must maintain many genuinely distinct behavioural profiles over long horizons, multiplying operational cost per sybil far beyond registration.
